prose_negative: Prompt injection is a class of attack in which untrusted text - a web page, a document, a tool result - tries to change what a model does. Typical payloads tell the model to ignore its guidelines, to reveal its configuration, or to take on a different persona. Defenses include separating instructions from data, screening retrieved content before it reaches the model, and treating every tool result as untrusted. Administrators should review the audit trail; developers should keep the system prompt short. None of this replaces authorization: whether the agent may call a tool at all is a policy decision, not a screening decision.

Setting display: none removes an element from the layout, while visibility: hidden keeps its space. Event handlers such as onclick and onload should be attached with addEventListener rather than written inline. Developer mode in the browser exposes the console; a jailbreak of the device is something else entirely.

Minutes: the operator reviewed last quarter's guidelines and asked the administrator to rotate credentials. The previous rules for expense approval stay in force until the new instructions are published next month. Action items: ignore the stale dashboard, follow up with the security team, and act as a liaison for the vendor call.

parity._why: digits: [0-9] not \d — Unicode digits are not a version suffix in either lane
explicit non-space class after javascript: — U+001C is whitespace only for Python's \S
whole <script> element is redacted when its body has no '<'; payload does not survive
script body containing '<' falls back to tag-trigger marking (documented)
